evidence.claim: The key evaluation metrics that accurately reflect model performance in imbalanced fraud detection scenarios
evidence.quote: The Classification Report delivers three essential metrics for evaluating our model's performance: 1. Precision (0.816 for Fraud): This means when our model predicts that a provider is fraudulent, it is correct 81.6% of the time. However, this indicates that about 18.4% of the flagged cases are false alarms. 2. Recall (0.385 for Fraud): Our model successfully identifies only 38.5% of actual fraud cases. This low recall suggests that the model is missing more than half of fraudulent instances, a trend also echoed in our confusion matrix results. 3. F1-Score (0.523 for Fraud): This score reflects the harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a balanced metric that factors in both false positives and false negatives. A score of 0.523 indicates that there is significant room for improvement in our fraud detection capabilities.
